content.title: Men’s March Madness 2026 Sweet 16 live updates: Duke, Michigan, UConn, Tennessee secure spots in Elite Eight
content.text: Follow our live coverage of the Sweet 16 action in the men’s NCAA TournamentTennessee celebrates after its Sweet 16 win. Getty ImagesLatest March Madness projections!Austin Mock's men’s NCAA Tournament projections are updated for the Elite Eight. The favorites this round:South: Illinois (71%)West: Arizona (56%)Midwest: Michigan (72%)East: Duke (66%)His title favorites: Favorites to win the men’s tournament Updated March 28, 2026 at 12:49 a.m. E.T. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementIowa State goes out with a whimper Getty Images A tough pill to swallow for a Cyclones team that more than held its own in the gauntlet of Big 12 men’s basketball this season. Not having Joshua Jefferson avaliable ultimately doomed Ohio State. Nate Heise played well in his place with 18 points, but Milan Momcilovic couldn’t deal with Tennessee’s pressure on him and finished with just six points on 2-of-9 shooting. Foul trouble stalled out what was otherwise an excellent night for guard Tamin Lipsey (18 points, 5 rebounds and 5 assists).Guards showed up for Vols, too Getty Images Both Ja'Kobi Gillespie and Nate Ament had things they needed to overcome tonight. Gillespie, Tennessee’s most reliable 3-point shooter, went a horrid 2-for-11 from deep. Ament was limited to 24 minutes after getting into foul trouble early in the second half. Despite that, Gillespie finished with 16 points, only topped by Amen, who had a game-high 18.Tennessee's bigs dominated Getty Images We wrote a lot during the game about how Tennessee obliterated Iowa State on the class, but the numbers are still staggering. Starting center Felix Okpara and backup Jaylen Carey had 10 rebounds, including six offensive rebounds — each. They also scored in double digits, with Okpara scoring 12 points and Carey notching 11. Iowa State simply had no answer for them in the paint. The final rebounding disparity was Vols plus-19 — Tennessee 43, Iowa State 22 — and 16-8 on the offensive boards.Tennessee looking to get rid of record Getty Images To add on to Scott's point below, Tennessee also has the most NCAA Tournament wins without a Final Four appearance with 34. They can put an end to that bittersweet stat with win number 35 against Michigan on Sunday.Barnes adds to all-time great resume Getty Images Remember when Rick Barnes had a reputation as a great regular-season coach who couldn’t get it done in the NCAA Tournament? Well, his team’s suffocating 76-62 win over Iowa State on Friday at United Center makes it three straight Elite Eights for Tennessee — a program that had one in its history before this streak.Bob Knight, among many other distinguished coaches, never reached three straight Elite Eights. The Midwest Region No. 6 seed Vols (25-11) have earned a Sunday shot at No. 1 seed Michigan (34-3) in an attempt to earn the program’s first Final Four and the second of Barnes’ career. The Vols’ chances hinge on a top-15 defense and an offensive rebounding rate that leads the nation. Better shooting — UT was just 7-for-22 from long range — would help as well.Oh, and Tennessee needs some luck. It got some Friday in the absence of Iowa State’s best player, forward Joshua Jefferson, who was out with a sprained ankle. The Cyclones (29-8) have been on an offensive tear of late but struggled mostly to find any space for the nation’s best shooter, Milan Momcilovic (2-for-9, 6 points). Tamin Lipsey scored 18 in his final game for Iowa State.Tennessee’s best player, freshman wing Nate Ament, seems to be getting healthier after struggling recently with his own ankle and knee situation. He hit a mid-range shot to push the lead to 11 with less than 3 minutes to play, then capped the night with a 3-point swish and finished with 18 points. Ja’Kobi Gillespie scored 16 and the Vols offset 17 turnovers with 16 offensive rebounds.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCan Tennessee get over the hump? Getty Images Tennessee ranks fourth among programs with the most NCAA tournament appearances without a Final Four appearance. In order, the dubious top-5 list includes:BYU 33Missouri 31Xavier 30Tennessee 28Creighton 26Iowa State missed Jefferson Getty Images Gotta feel for Iowa State’s Joshua Jefferson. He hadn’t missed a game in his two seasons with the Cyclones before his injury in the first round of this year’s NCAA Tournament. Have to think he would have had an impact on this game if he were healthy enough to play.Izzo heaps praise on UConn Getty Images Tom Izzo is giving a lot of credit not just to UConn's top players, but its reserve guards and wings: 💬 “(Malachi) Smith dogs you. And Jayden Ross is a hell of a player.”Izzo continued: 💬 “The better team won tonight. (Danny Hurley’s) done a hell of a job. He's got some guys who have played for national championships ... But we didn't take a backseat today.”Izzo shuts down questions of retirement Getty Images Don't count on Tom Izzo retiring anytime soon. Asked where he sees himself in five years, Izzo is unequivocal:💬 “Trying to win a national championship. Plain and simple. That's it. And those things usually start after your lost loss. Nowadays it's a little more screwed up, but not at Michigan State ... I'm feeling good. We talk about retirement, why? What the hell am I gonna do?”Ament on Tennessee’s win Getty ImagesNate Ament on the TBS broadcast after his 18-point performance to help Tennessee return to the Elite Eight:💬 “Just my teammates believing in me. They make my job so much easier when they believe in me and want me to take over the game. My confidence is their confidence.“Just never letting up, doing what we do in practice and letting it translate to the game. We’re gonna be who we are no matter the opponent.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementIzzo defends Fears Getty ImagesJeremy Fears Jr. on Michigan State getting down 19 in the first half: 💬 “We just didn't do our part early. That falls on us. That falls on me ... I didn't really answer the bell for the guys.”Tom Izzo, visibly emotional, interjects: 💬 “I wouldn't say that.”Izzo: 'We kind of wore down' Getty ImagesMore from Tom Izzo:💬 “We just kind of wore down ... Lot of credit to Danny and his team. I like his team. He's got an inside guy that can score, some guards. But I thought our guys played their asses off.”Russo's insights on Duke's winYour browser does not support the video tag.Earlier tonight, No. 1 Duke outlasted No. 5 St. John's in a thriller to advance to the Elite Eight. The Red Storm led by 10 points in the second half but were unable to hold off a Blue Devil's surge.Check out additional analysis from Ralph Russo of The Athletic here.Izzo discusses MSU's loss Getty ImagesTom Izzo after Michigan St.'s loss to UConn: “It's very hard to be disappointed yet proud ... We said they'd come out and punch us in the mouth, and they did.”TNT reporter draped in towels TNT SportsEvan Washburn is under there somewhere.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUConn's seniors shined Getty ImagesWith a spot in the Elite Eight on the line, the Huskies leaned heavily on their experienced players to help get them across the finish line.Alex Karaban and Tarris Reed Jr. combined for 37 points, each making a pair of clutch free throws down the stretch to close out the win. The duo also combined for 12 rebounds and seven assists.Tonight marks Karaban's 16th tourney win Getty ImagesDan Hurley is reminded that tonight is Alex Karaban's 16th NCAA Tournament win, the third-most all-time behind only Christian Laettner and... Hurley's brother, Bobby."Oh, Bob. How many did he have?"19, Hurley is told. Laettner had 21. Karaban can only tie Bobby Hurley if UConn wins its third championship in four seasons."Yeah, my brother was so good."FINAL: Tennessee back in Elite 8! Getty ImagesFinal - Tennessee 76, Iowa State 62Make that THREE straight Elite 8 trips for Rick Barnes and Tennessee! The Volunteers will face Michigan on Sunday with a spot in the Final Four on the line!Karaban on clutch free throwsA reporter asked UConn forward Alex Karaban how he tries to compose himself before late-game free-throws, knowing his season and college career are hanging in the balance. Karaban just busts out in a goofy grin:“I don't think that much at the free-throw line.”
